\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{طلایی} (talâyi)}{طلایی (talâyi)}]{\fa{طلایی} (talâyi) — golden}

\label{lesson:FA-C128-talayi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for purple, then the Persian for grey.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{طلایی}}
\textbf{\fa{طلایی}} — \emph{talâyi} — \textquotedblleft{}golden\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{talâyi} is \emph{talâ}, \textquotedblleft{}gold\textquotedblright{}, with the colour ending \emph{-i}. \emph{talâ} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṭilāʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}coating, gilding\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{ṭ-l-y}, Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گرد} (gerd)}{گرد (gerd)}]{\fa{گرد} (gerd) — round}

\label{lesson:FA-C128-gerd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for grey, then the Persian for golden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گرد}}
\textbf{\fa{گرد}} — \emph{gerd} — \textquotedblleft{}round\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gerd} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{gird}, \textquotedblleft{}round\textquotedblright{}. EtymDB takes it back to the Indo-European root \emph{*wert-}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{}, the root of Latin \emph{vertere}. (It also lists \emph{gard}, \textquotedblleft{}dust\textquotedblright{}, a different word.)
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مهربان} (mehrabân)}{مهربان (mehrabân)}]{\fa{مهربان} (mehrabân) — kind}

\label{lesson:FA-C128-mehraban}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for golden, then the Persian for round.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مهربان}}
\textbf{\fa{مهربان}} — \emph{mehrabân} — \textquotedblleft{}kind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mehrabân} is \emph{mehr}, \textquotedblleft{}love, kindness\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-bân}, \textquotedblleft{}keeper\textquotedblright{}: one who keeps kindness. EtymDB traces it to Middle Persian \emph{mihrbān}. \emph{mehr} is also the name of the old god Mithra.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آرام} (ârâm)}{آرام (ârâm)}]{\fa{آرام} (ârâm) — calm, quiet}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آرام}}
\textbf{\fa{آرام}} — \emph{ârâm} — \textquotedblleft{}calm, quiet\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}
